items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: I knew who Dan was because he was from southern California, Dan Barrett. And I think Dan and I had met on the bandstand a couple of times in California... friends of ours: Dan Barrett

ctx.x: As Dan Barrett said, taking about, someone asked him about modes. He said, “Well all knowledge is good, you just have to know when to use it or not.”

Well and Dan’s point is well taken. I mean there’s a lot of things that I learned about that I don’t really have any use for. I think it’s more of just the discipline of having learned them. Sure, in one of the schools I went to I had a great teacher who taught me many © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

wonderful things about what you could play over a G7 that had absolutely nothing to do with G7, but is that information that I use in my gigs? No. Not really. But there’s still a math to it, and there’s still a lens to learn how to listen through music through certain lenses. There’s still ways to learn how to do that. And any time you’re introduced to something new and can return to those methods and be more efficient at it, even if it’s not — whether it’s information you’re going to use or not use, you’re still…
